name: Breakout
caption: Your D has just picked up the puck behind your net and is turning up ice to the {side}. Their first forechecker is about 20 feet away and closing.

questions.prompt: Your D is turning up ice toward your side. What do you do?

options.text: Get to the right half-wall, stop, face the D with my forehand open, and call for it.
options.feedback: Yes. Be there before he turns up ice, stopped, so he sees a target and not a moving guess. Decide chip, carry or reverse before the puck arrives.

options.text: Skate up through the half-wall toward the blue line so I am moving when the pass comes.
options.feedback: Then the pass has to lead a moving target through the forechecker. If it misses, you are the one furthest from the puck.

options.text: Go low to help my D behind the net.
options.feedback: That is the center’s job. Two helpers low and nobody on the wall means there is no outlet when he turns.

options.text: Cut into the middle to give him a pass up the gut.
options.feedback: The center is already filling the middle. Your job is width; two players in the middle makes the wall pass impossible.

questions.prompt: Your D is turning up ice away from your side. What do you do?

options.text: Hold my half-wall but start up ice slowly, so I am the weak-side option for a cross-ice or a chip to the far side.
options.feedback: Good. When the breakout goes the other way, the weak-side winger is the second wave: wide, timing it so you hit the blue line with speed if the puck comes across.

options.text: Stop on my half-wall, face my D and wait.
options.feedback: Fine on the strong side, but on the weak side a stopped winger is nowhere near the play. Stay wide, but start moving.

options.text: Skate across to the puck side to give him a closer option.
options.feedback: Now both wingers and the center are on one half of the ice, and the whole far side is empty for them to pinch into.

options.text: Go straight to the blue line and wait for a stretch pass.
options.feedback: Through a forechecker and two D? Realistically that pass does not get there, and you are offside the moment it does.

questions.prompt: Tap where you want to be when your D looks up.
questions.label: Half-wall

fb.right: The half-wall, stopped, forehand to the puck. Exactly where he expects you.
fb.close: Nearly: tighter to the boards and level with the hash marks. The D is looking for a target on the wall, not a guess in the middle.
fb.wrong: He is turning up ice toward you. Your spot is the right half-wall, stopped, before he looks.

questions.prompt: Tap where you want to be when your D looks up.
questions.label: Weak-side lane

fb.right: Right: wide on your side, a little higher than the half-wall, already drifting up ice as the weak-side option.
fb.close: Close. Keep the width, just a bit higher than you tapped so you can hit the line with speed when it comes across.
fb.wrong: The breakout goes the other way, so you are the second wave. Stay wide on your side and start moving up, rather than coming to the puck.
